Nutrition Diagnosis
Common nutritional problems associated with HIV/AIDS
include: increased energy expenditure; inadequate oral food/
beverage intake; excessive bioactive substances; increased 
nutrient needs; malnutrition; inadequate protein-energy intake;
swallowing diﬃ  culty; altered GI function; impaired nutrient 
utilization; altered nutrition-related laboratory values; food-
medication interaction; underweight; involuntary weight loss; 
impaired ability to prepare foods/meals; physical inactivity; and
intake of unsafe food.
